payload.name: PropagateEstablishedLocationToNewEvents
payload.description: When extracting a new event for a person already known to be at a specific location from earlier context, include that location in the memory if the event occurs there and no new location is stated.
content: During extraction, before writing an event memory, check prior conversation and existing memories for an active location associated with the subject.
If the new event (e.g., an activity or discovery) continues that known stay or trip and the message gives no different location, include the established location in the extracted memory content.
Do not invent a location when the known location and the event are not connected by time or travel context.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction sometimes records an activity while dropping its location when the location is not repeated in the triggering message. This causes later factual questions about where an event happened to be unanswerable from memory. The reusable mechanism is failure to carry an established location from earlier context into newly extracted events. The rule applies to any multi-turn conversation where a subject remains in a known place and mentions subsequent events there without restating the place.

payload.name: Preserve concrete planned activities in event extractions
payload.description: When extracting a planned event or meeting, if participants explicitly propose concrete activities, items, or food/drinks to try, include those specifics in the memory instead of a generic label.
content: During extraction of a planned event or meeting, include every explicitly proposed concrete activity, item, or experience (e.g., trying fresh pastries, coffee, a specific dish) in the memory content.
If the concrete detail appears in a separate message from the meeting arrangement, combine them into one event memory rather than dropping the detail.
Use the specific nouns and verbs from the evidence; do not reduce an activity detail to a generic topic label.

candidates.solves: When extracting a planned event or meeting, the agent may summarize it with a generic label and drop explicitly proposed concrete activities or items, causing memories that only partially cover later claims. This rule applies to any plan/event extraction where participants name specific things they intend to do, eat, try, or bring; those details must be preserved even if they appear in separate messages.

payload.name: Extract-travel-location-period-facts
payload.description: When a message ties a person to a past travel or vacation location and a time period, extract a state/event candidate even if the location is mentioned in passing.
content: Create an event/state extraction candidate whenever a message associates a person with a location during a time period (e.g., a trip, vacation, visit, stay, or residence), even if that association is incidental to the message's main topic.
Resolve relative time references like 'last summer' or 'last year' to absolute dates using the message/session timestamp and record the resolved period.
When the location is a city with an unambiguous country, store both so country-level questions remain answerable.

candidates.solves: Extraction produced no candidate for a clear location-period fact ('vacation last summer in Bogota'), so it was never persisted. The missing rule is to emit state/event candidates from narrative travel/vacation mentions that tie a person, place, and time; resolve relative time to absolute dates; and include the unambiguous country. Applies to future messages containing person-location-time associations; not to hypothetical/future plans or time-less place mentions.

payload.name: Aggregate repeated location visits into count memory
payload.description: Use when a subject's visits/trips to the same city, country, or place are mentioned across multiple messages, and a memory storing the total number of visits should be created or updated.
content: When extracting candidates from a message, if the message describes a visit or trip to a location already mentioned as visited by the same subject in an existing memory, extract a candidate that records the total number of visits to that location (or updates an existing visit-count event), not only a new separate event.

During CRUD, when a candidate or existing memory contains a visit to a location and another memory records a different visit to the same location by the same subject, update or merge into one event memory that explicitly states the combined visit count.

candidates.solves: When a person's visits to the same city or country appear in more than one message, the extraction stage often records each visit as a separate event and never stores the total count, so later count questions cannot be answered from memory. This Skill instructs the agent to aggregate repeated location-visit mentions into one explicit count memory (or update an existing one), making visit-count facts durable and queryable. It applies during candidate extraction and during CRUD when merging memory candidates.

payload.name: Resolve named venue locations during extraction
payload.description: When extracting plan/event memories from messages that mention a named venue or franchise with well-known locations, include those possible locations (e.g., states) explicitly.
content: During extraction, if a message mentions a named destination (e.g., theme park, stadium, landmark, chain) whose geographic location(s) are widely known, include the resolved location(s) (e.g., 'California or Florida') in the candidate content, even if the user did not state them. If the venue has multiple known sites, list the possible states explicitly. Only use well-established facts; avoid speculative or obscure inferences.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause: extraction captured a plan to visit a named theme park but omitted the park's well-known geographic locations, leaving a later location query unsupported. The reusable mechanism is that named venues or franchises carry established location facts that should be included in extracted plan/event memories. Future inputs mentioning any well-known destination—theme parks, stadiums, landmarks, or chains—should trigger this location-resolving rule.

payload.name: Extract how the user discovered an event as a separate memory
payload.description: When a user states how they heard about or discovered an event, place, or opportunity (saw a flyer, friend referral, online ad), extract that discovery as its own memory candidate during extraction.
content: During extraction, when the user explicitly states how they learned about an event or opportunity (e.g., saw a flyer, heard from a friend, found an ad), create a separate event memory capturing the discovery source, in addition to any memory of the event itself.
Set memory_kind to 'event', subject to the speaker, and world_start to the session timestamp; include the concrete source and place (e.g., 'at the local pet store').
Keep discovery-source memories distinct from the main event memory; do not merge them, so future questions such as 'How did X hear about Y?' have supporting evidence.

candidates.solves: The extraction stage recorded the workshop enrollment and a related meeting but omitted the user's explicit statement that she saw a workshop flyer at her local pet store, so 'how did she hear about it' became unanswerable. The reusable pattern is that any explicit disclosure of a discovery source (flyer, referral, advertisement, online post) for an event or opportunity is a distinct durable fact that should be extracted independently whenever such a statement appears. It does not apply to opinions, preferences, or details already fully captured by an existing memory.

payload.name: Extract all explicitly stated plan elements
payload.description: When a plan or event is described across multiple messages, retrieve this Skill to ensure each explicitly named activity or detail is captured during candidate extraction.
content: During extraction, treat each explicitly stated element of a plan or event (activity, item, time, participant) as an extractable fact, even if it appears in an earlier message than the message that most clearly names the plan.

When multiple messages jointly describe one plan, either include all explicitly mentioned elements in a single candidate's content or create one candidate per element; never let a later, more prominent mention cause earlier distinct details to be omitted.

candidates.solves: When multiple messages jointly define a plan, extraction may keep only the later salient message and drop earlier explicit elements, causing supported claims to be missing from memory. The rule requires persisting all explicitly named elements of a plan, not just the last mention. It applies to future sessions where several messages together state a plan's components, but not to inferring unstated details.
